qr.note: The login *process* id travels as `login_id` at the top level — the same word mautrix's ?login_id= query parameter uses for an existing login. `txn_id` is issued here and validated on the call that advances this step. `display_and_wait` carries only `type` and `data`; there is no `can_cancel`, and the bridge renders no image.
substituted: display_and_wait.data is a placeholder of the real length and prefix: the real value is a WhatsApp pairing credential

body.instructions: Scan the QR code with the WhatsApp mobile app to log in

phone.note: The other WhatsApp flow. `instructions` is an empty string rather than absent, and `user_input.attachments` is explicitly null. `fields[].id` is the key the submitted body must carry.

fields.name: Phone number
fields.description: Your WhatsApp phone number in international format

unknown_flow.note: POST /login/start/definitely-not-a-flow. WhatsApp does not validate the flow id: it silently gives you the QR flow. Signal answers 404 M_NOT_FOUND for the same call. A flow-id typo is therefore invisible on one bridge and fatal on the other.

body.instructions: Scan the QR code with the WhatsApp mobile app to log in

body.error: User does not have login permissions
